textbookText: 4. How is electricity produced from generator? Describe with well labelled diagram. Ans:- A generator is a device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. It works on the principle of electromagnetic induction. When a rectangular coil is rotated mechanically between the poles of a strong magnet, the magnetic flux linked with the coil changes continuously. Due to this change in magnetic flux, an induced emf is produced in the coil, causing electric current to flow in the external circuit. In an AC generator, slip rings are used to obtain alternating current. A generator works on the principle of electromagnetic induction, which states that an electric current is induced in a conductor when it cuts magnetic lines of force. 5. Study the given diagram and answer the following questions. i) Write the working mechanism of the device shown in the diagram. Ans:- When the bicycle wheel rotates, it turns the roller of the dynamo, which rotates a magnet inside a coil wound on a soft iron core. Due to the rotation of the magnet, the magnetic flux linked with the coil changes continuously, inducing an alternating current in the coil. This current flows through the circuit and lights the bicycle lamp. ii) On which principle does it base? Ans:- It is based on the principle of electromagnetic induction. iii) Write any two methods by which we can increase the amount of current produced by it. Ans:- Any two methods to increase the amount of current produced are,
1. By increasing the speed of rotation of the magnet (i.e., riding the bicycle faster). 2. By increasing the number of turns of the coil.
6. Sketch a labelled schematic diagram of a step-up transformer and explain how it helps to increase potential difference.
Ans:- A step-up transformer works on the principle of electromagnetic
induction and is used to increase the potential difference of an alternating
current. When an AC voltage is applied to the primary coil, which has fewer
turns, it produces a continuously changing magnetic flux in the laminated soft
iron core. This changing magnetic flux links with the secondary coil, which
has a greater number of turns, and induces an alternating emf in it. Since the
number of turns in the secondary coil is more than that in the primary coil, the
induced voltage in the secondary becomes higher than the input voltage.
Hence, a step-up transformer increases the potential difference while the
current decreases correspondingly.
7. In the given diagram C2 has 1/5 coil of C1. If the input voltage is 1200V, what will be the
output voltage? What is the reason behind laminating the core of this device?
(Ans: 240 V)
Ans:- Given, Primary voltage (𝑉𝑝) = 1200V
Primary turns (𝑁𝑝) = C1
Secondary voltage (𝑉𝑆) = ? Secondary turns (𝑁𝑠) = C1/5 We know that, 𝑉𝑆 𝑉𝑝 = 𝑁𝑠 𝑁𝑝 or, 𝑉𝑆 1200𝑣 = 𝐶1/5 𝐶1 or, 𝑉𝑆 = 1200V/5 = 240V
Therefore, output voltage is 240V.
The core of the transformer is laminated to reduce energy loss due to eddy currents, which are induced in the core by the
changing magnetic flux. Lamination increases the resistance of the core and thereby minimizes heating and power loss,
improving the efficiency of the transformer.
8. A transformer is shown in the figure.
i) Label the parts A and B.
Ans:- In the given figure A is primary winding and B is secondary winding.
ii) Which type of transformer is it and why?
Ans:- The given figure is step up transformer because secondary winding has more turns than the primary
winding.
iii) ‘The use of alternating current (a.c.) is limited without transformer.’ Justify it.
Ans:- The use of alternating current (a.c.) would be limited without a transformer because a transformer makes it possible to
change the voltage of a.c. easily. By using a step-up transformer, the voltage can be increased for long-distance transmission,
which reduces current and hence minimizes power loss due to heating in transmission wires. Similarly, a step-down
transformer reduces high transmission voltage to a safe and suitable level for domestic and industrial use. Without
transformers, efficient long-distance transmission and safe utilization of a.c. would not be possible, greatly limiting its
practical use.
9. What type of transformer is shown in the diagram? What substance is used to laminate of this
core? Find out the voltage produced in the secondary coil in the given diagram. (Ans: 440V)
Ans:- Step up transformer is shown in the given diagram. The transformer core is laminated using
thin sheets of soft iron (silicon steel).
Given, Primary voltage (𝑉𝑝) = 220V
Primary turns (𝑁𝑝) = 250 turns
Secondary voltage (𝑉𝑆) = ? Secondary turns (𝑁𝑠) = 500 turns We know that, 𝑉𝑆 𝑉𝑝 = 𝑁𝑠 𝑁𝑝 or, 𝑉𝑆 220𝑣 = 500 250 or, 𝑉𝑆 = 220 * 2 V = 440V
Therefore, output voltage is 440V.
